question: On synth-1m, is realised 1-minute volatility higher in the first 30 minutes after the 09:30 New York cash open than in the rest of the same session? Report the mean over sessions of the ratio of realised volatility in that window to realised volatility in the rest of the session as the statistic `open_vol_ratio`, and test the hypothesis that the window is more volatile at the 5% level.

plan.hypothesis: On synth-1m, realised 1-minute volatility in the 09:30-10:00 New York window is higher than realised 1-minute volatility in the rest of the same session, i.e. the mean over sessions of the per-minute volatility ratio exceeds 1.
plan.method: 1. Load synth-1m (single symbol SYN), convert ts from UTC to America/New_York so the 09:30 open tracks DST. 2. Assign each bar to a session using the dataset's 18:00-17:00 NY session: session date = NY calendar date of (ts_ny + 6 hours), so bars from 18:00 belong to the next day's session. 3. Compute 1-minute log returns r_t = ln(close_t / close_{t-1}) within a session only: drop the first bar of every session (its return spans the 17:00-18:00 break) and drop any return whose bar is at or straddles a contract switch timestamp (all 12 switches fall exactly at 09:30 NY, so the switch-day 09:30 return would otherwise mix two contracts). 4. Window = bars with NY time in [09:30, 10:00) (30 returns, the first being 09:29 close to 09:30 close); rest = every other return in the same session (18:00 previous evening to 16:59, excluding the window). 5. Per session, realised volatility is normalised per minute so the two windows of very different length are comparable: RV_window = sqrt(mean of r^2 over window), RV_rest = sqrt(mean of r^2 over rest). 6. Keep sessions with a full 30-return window (29 on switch days after the drop) and at least 90% of the expected rest returns; report how many sessions are kept and dropped. 7. ratio_s = RV_window / RV_rest per session; open_vol_ratio = mean of ratio_s over kept sessions. Also report the median ratio, the share of sessions with ratio > 1, and mean of ln(ratio_s) as robustness.
plan.significance: One-sided test of H0: E[ratio_s] <= 1 against H1: E[ratio_s] > 1, using a t-test on the per-session ratios with Newey-West HAC standard errors (lag 5 sessions, to allow for volatility clustering across days), at the 5% level. Robustness: the same one-sided HAC test on ln(ratio_s) > 0.

summary.text: Yes. On synth-1m, realised 1-minute volatility in the first 30 minutes after the 09:30 New York open was about twice that of the rest of the same session. The mean per-session ratio open_vol_ratio is 1.997 (95% CI 1.981 to 2.013, n = 783 sessions). The one-sided Newey-West test rejects H0: ratio <= 1 at the 5% level (t about 122, p < 0.001). Every session had a ratio above 1.
